ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is labeled kinetic energy, and the vertical axis is labeled Number of SO2 molecules. The curve rises from the low kinetic energy region, reaches its highest point near the letter B, then gradually decreases to the right and forms a longer right-side tail. The letters A, B, C, D are arranged along the horizontal axis from left to right, where B is located below the peak, C is located to the right of the peak, and D is farther to the right, in the sparse tail region. Reasoning: The highest point of this distribution represents the most probable kinetic energy, so B is the most probable kinetic energy. Since the curve is skewed to the right, the average kinetic energy will be pulled to the right of the peak by the long tail on the right, but will not fall at the very far sparse tail end. Among the given letters, C is located to the right of the peak and not too deep into the tail, so it represents the average kinetic energy.
